title: Belgium's CCB runs third "Hack the Government" event, with twelve government sites tested by ethical hackers
date_note: La Libre, published 27 November, says the event ran "this week" and gives no exact days.
summary: La Libre reports that twelve government websites were hacked legally this week in the third "Hack the Government" event run by the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium (CCB). Près de 77 participants, including 32 students and 45 hackers, tested the systems, and nearly twice as many vulnerability reports were recorded as last year. CCB director Miguel De Bruycker says a flaw is better found by a trusted researcher than by a malicious actor.
plain: Belgium's cybersecurity centre let ethical hackers legally test twelve government websites this week. Près de 77 participants took part, and nearly twice as many vulnerability reports came in as last year, La Libre reports.
exec: La Libre reports that Belgium's CCB tested twelve government sites with près de 77 participants; the CCB's director says a trusted researcher finding a flaw beats a malicious actor finding it.
geo_basis: country only; the page names no city, pinned at Brussels as the capital
